name: Chicken Parmesan Pasta
intro_html: Chicken parm is a restaurant order that usually comes with a restaurant price. This meal-prep version skips the breading and the deep fryer but keeps everything you actually love: tender chicken, marinara, and a blanket of melty cheese over high-protein pasta. At {{protein}} grams of protein a bowl for about ${{cost_ps}} (at everyday cost), it is a filling, high-protein dinner.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 3.5 lb raw: ~$7.80. Buy 4 lbs: $8.92.
Penne Pasta, 7 1/4 cups (14.5 oz each): ~$3.83. Buy 2 14.5oz boxes: $4.38.
Reduced Fat Mozzarella, 1 3/4 cups shredded: ~$1.50. Buy 1 8oz bag: $1.74.
Pantry seasonings (italian seasoning, salt, black pepper, garlic powder): ~$0.64. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $18.84 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.35 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $26.07 across 14 servings, roughly $1.86 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $11.34 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $37.41. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a chicken parm that would run $16 or more at a sit-down spot.
shop_smart: Chicken on sale, frozen, is the move that quietly lowers the cost of half the recipes on this site.
A little parmesan goes far. One container covers several batches, so the per-serving cost stays tiny.
Store-brand sauce and cheese save a couple dollars with no difference on the plate.

Get the protein penne the ingredient list asks for. The box is 14.5 ounces, not the pound box plain pasta comes in, so check the count before you get to the register. It costs more than ordinary dried pasta, and the store brand runs cheaper than the name brand where you can get it.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the penne to al dente per the box, then drain.

Cube the chicken, season it with the salt, black pepper, and Italian seasoning, and cook in a large skillet with the olive oil over medium-high heat until it reaches 165F inside. Stir in the minced garlic for the last minute.
Pour in the pasta sauce and simmer a couple of minutes until hot.
Add the drained penne and stir to coat, then fold in the parmesan.
Melt the butter in a small skillet, stir in the panko breadcrumbs and garlic powder, and toast, stirring often, until golden and crisp.
Scatter the mozzarella over the pasta and cover for a minute until it melts, then shower the toasted panko over the top.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container. Every bowl lands near {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein.

recipeIngredient: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Penne Pasta, 7 1/4 cups (14.5 oz each) (719 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella, 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
steps: Boil the penne to al dente and drain.
Season the cubed chicken with salt, black pepper, and Italian seasoning, cook it in the olive oil to 165F, and stir in the garlic at the end.
Add the pasta sauce and simmer until hot, then stir in the penne and fold in the parmesan.
Toast the panko breadcrumbs and garlic powder in the melted butter until golden.
Top with mozzarella until melted, shower on the toasted panko, and divide into 14 containers.
